verify_command: python3 -B src/gen/verify_inventory.py <tree> --pin <manifest_sha256> (the verifier is also in LRI_C8_D2_HPC/gen/)
d_pipeline: The builder bodies (masks, terms, forests, weights, statuses) do not depend on d and come from gen/build_free and gen/build_power. The rate line (last line of a G-file) is the only d-dependent part: these builders write it at d=2 (parity rule, rate[S] = max(|S| odd ? 1 : 2, twice[S])/2 for 0 < S < 2^E - 1, and 0 at S = 0 and S = 2^E - 1); the d=3 rate line is rewritten from these d=2 G-files by C63d's regenerate_rates.cpp. The builders take no d parameter (DECISIONS.md C1, acknowledged by C63d on 2026-10-03).
checksum_hierarchy: G-file members -> MEMBERS.sha256; every file except MANIFEST.json and SHA256SUMS -> SHA256SUMS; SHA256SUMS -> MANIFEST.json (sha256sums_sha256); MANIFEST.json is pinned only from outside the tree (HANDOFF_inventory8_d2.json). Verify a copy with gen/verify_inventory.py TREE --pin <sha256 of MANIFEST.json>.
member_layout: payload/<stem>.tar holds <stem>/G<id>.txt, id = class id in classesL.txt; text G-files, magic C7D2GRAPH1, the C7(2) format
r2_procedure: inventory8_d2/ is never modified. A defect found after H1 (by C63d's gates 1-7, by C62d's tests or later) is handled by publishing inventory8_d2_r2/ with a new MANIFEST sha256 and a SUPERSEDES.json naming the defect and the affected classes; this HANDOFF file is then updated and both packages re-pin; C62d reruns A-IN-3..5 and A-RPL-7 on the affected kernels. Campaigns planned against r1 keep their inputs-manifest pin, so merge and assemble refuse them under the r2 package; they stay usable only with the commit they were planned with.
